title: Darren Baker is latest Giants addition with franchise bloodlines
content:
PITTSBURGH — The San Francisco Giants traded for Jeff Kent’s son and drafted Barry Bonds’ nephew. Now they’re signing another player with a high-profile connection to the 2002 World Series team.

Their famous former batboy.

The team has agreed to a Triple-A contract with infielder Darren Baker, the son of former manager Dusty Baker, a team source confirmed to The Athletic. The source spoke anonymously because the contract, which was first reported by NBC Sports Bay Area, is pending a physical.

Baker, 27, is a left-handed-hitting second baseman and left fielder who made his major-league debut with the Washington Nationals in 2024. He signed a minor-league contract with the Chicago White Sox before this season but played in just 11 games for Triple-A Charlotte before a back injury sidelined him.

If you couldn’t digest any of the details in that last paragraph after reading that Baker is 27, you’re forgiven. Yes, it’s really been almost a quarter-century since 3-year-old Darren served as a batboy in that 2002 World Series, which ended in heartbreak with road losses in Game 6 and Game 7 to the Anaheim Angels.

The Giants had positioned themselves to clinch with a rollicking 16-4 victory in San Francisco, and the manager’s son was at the center of Game 5’s most memorable moment. He had toddled out to collect Kenny Lofton’s bat — Lofton hit a two-run triple off the brick arcade — and was about to cross in front of the plate when J.T. Snow, who was running from second base, caught Darren by the jacket and yanked him out of harm’s way. Snow was hailed as a hero for avoiding a potential collision with David Bell, who was also sprinting home.

Darren Baker went on to play at Cal and was the Nationals’ 10th-round draft pick in 2021. After making his major-league debut, he was 7-for-14 with two doubles in a nine-game cameo.

Reporting to Sacramento will be a homecoming of sorts for Baker, who grew up in the area and played at Jesuit High in Carmichael, Calif.

The Giants added a catcher and another pitcher when the roster expanded to 28 players Tuesday, recalling Zach Morgan as a third-stringer behind the plate and selecting left-hander Cesar Perdomo from Sacramento. They already have left-handed hitting Nate Furman on the major-league roster, and they still expect infielder Marcelo Mayer to be ready to play at some point this month, so there’s no guarantee Baker will get a chance to wear a Giants uniform again. If he does, though, it’ll be a few sizes larger than his last one.

The Giants really are leaning into their bloodlines. Within a week of Kent’s induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame, the Giants acquired his son, Kaeden, from the New York Yankees along with left-handed prospect Henry Lanane for outfielder Heliot Ramos. Kaeden Kent made his debut with Single-A Eugene on Aug. 26 and hit two home runs in his second game. They also took Barry Bonds’ nephew, Peyton, with their third-round pick in this year’s draft. Peyton Bonds is a power-hitting outfielder from Rutgers. In both cases, Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey said his staff liked both players primarily for their skills and not because of their famous names.
